question: Is SIBAL fabric safe in the lunar surface habitat at 10 cm/s?
behavior: Lunar gravity (and 8.2 psia / 34% O2) has no training data, so the OOD warning must be the first line.

OOD first line.detail: ⚠️ Out of distribution: no training data at this gravity lev

answer:
⚠️ Out of distribution: no training data at this gravity level (the dataset is ISS microgravity only; no long-duration fire experiment has been done in actual lunar gravity yet, NASA FM2 is planned to be the first); pressure 8.2 psia outside training range 14.4–15 psia (1 atm ± 0.3 psia, every BASS-II test); O2 34% outside the tested range for SIBAL fabric (16.4–21%).

**Verdict**
The prediction engine returns an out-of-distribution warning, so no definitive safety verdict can be established. SIBAL fabric tests in the training database are limited to ISS microgravity (1 g gravity level is unsupported), near-ambient pressure (14.4–15 psia), and lower oxygen concentrations (16.4–21% O₂). 

**Key numbers**
- Flow velocity: 10 cm/s
- Oxygen concentration: 34% (Preset: Lunar surface habitat)
- Pressure: 8.2 psia (56.5 kPa)
- Gravity: lunar (0.166 g)
- Tested O₂ range for SIBAL fabric: 16.4–21% O₂
- Training pressure range: 14.4–15 psia

**Evidence**
Nearest matching BASS-II baseline experiments (tested at 1 atm, microgravity, 21% O₂):
- **GMT96-T7**: SIBAL fabric, 10 cm/s flow, 21% O₂, 14.7 psia, microgravity — **burn** (steady spread rate observed)
- **GMT96-T8**: SIBAL fabric, 5 cm/s flow, 21% O₂, 14.7 psia, microgravity — **burn**
- **GMT100-T5**: SIBAL fabric, 10 cm/s flow, 18.8% O₂, 14.7 psia, microgravity — **burn**

**Operational recommendation**
Because this condition falls entirely outside the validated envelope (higher oxygen and reduced pressure in lunar gravity), apply conservative margin controls: limit the amount of exposed SIBAL fabric, strictly isolate potential ignition sources, and ensure fire detection and suppression systems remain active. This is decision support, not a replacement for NASA-STD-6001 material testing.

**Limits**
All training data for SIBAL fabric comes exclusively from ISS microgravity tests at ambient 1 atm pressure and lower oxygen percentages. No long-duration fire experiments have been conducted in partial lunar gravity.

nearest_experiments.evidence_quote: Figure 7.2 shows flame development stages of a 2.2-cm sample in 10-cm/s flow and 21 percent O2. Figure 7.2(a) shows side-view flame tracking of flame tip, flame base, and flame length. Figure 7.2(b) shows flame edge-view video still images at different stages. Note in the figure, flow is from right to left. After the igniter was turned on, a strong flame was initiated on both sides of the solid fuel. The flame was stabilized and started to grow and move downstream. At about 19 s, the flame reached a limiting constant length and a steady spread rate relative to the laboratory

Figure 7.3 shows flame development stages of a 2.2-cm sample in 5-cm/s flow and 21 percent O2. Unlike the flame in 10-cm/s flow in Figure 7.2, the flame from the side-view video is very dim in this case. Figure 7.3 thus shows the top-view images and tracking from those images. Because the flow speed is lower, it took more than 60 s to burn the whole sample. Steady spread time lasts for about 21 s
ignited at 10, turned down to 2, then 1, sample very small and dim, but seemed to burn full sample length as a flamelet
